title: Flat, finitely presented, separated, quasi-finite morphisms are finite locally free on a stratification (Stacks 07RZ)
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Then there exist closed subsets $\emptyset=Z_{-1}\subseteq Z_0\subseteq Z_1\subseteq Z_2\subseteq\cdots\subseteq S$ such that, with $S_r=Z_r\setminus Z_{r-1}$ ($r\geq0$), the sets $S_r$ are pairwise disjoint with union $S=\coprod_{r\ge0}S_r$, and this stratification has the following universal property: for every morphism of schemes $g:T\to S$, the projection $X\times_ST\to T$ (fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]) is finite locally free of degree $r$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free] if and only if $g(T)\subseteq S_r$ (as sets). Moreover, each inclusion $S_r\to S$ is quasi-compact, i.e. $S_r\cap W$ is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open $W\subseteq S$. (Stacks Project, More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 07RZ.)

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 07RZ (lemma-stratify-flat-fp-qf), line 12845, with its proof (uses Morphisms Lemma 03JA and More on Morphisms Lemma 07RY)

proof.text: Obtain local quasi-finiteness and a universal fibre-degree bound from quasi-finiteness and quasi-compactness, then use the bounded affine stratification theorem pointwise to define the global filtration by degree sublevel sets.
The bounded theorem gives closed sublevel loci, disjoint degree strata, their cover, and the universal finite-locally-free criterion.

Induct on the lower degree to show upper degree loci meet quasi-compact opens compactly; the affine successor step is isolated as the separately stated descent theorem. Intersect the compact upper locus with the closed sublevel locus to obtain compactness of each degree stratum.

proof_origin.place: affine bounded stratification plus induction on upper degree loci

split_report.summary: Statement checked against Stacks 07RZ (more-morphisms.tex line 12845) and kept. Proof follows the two paragraphs of the Stacks proof in ten steps. First paragraph ('local on S; 03JA; 07RY'): restriction of f to an affine open W is again flat, lfp, separated, quasi-finite with quasi-compact source, so its fibres are universally bounded (existing node 03JA); 07RY (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-flat-fp-lqf-bounded-stratification, stated with the 03J4 bound inline and S_r empty for r > n) stratifies W; the gluing that Stacks leaves implicit is written out: the strata are characterized pointwise by the universal property at Spec kappa(s), so they agree on overlaps, Z_r is closed because it is closed in every affine open, and the universal property is checked on the cover g^{-1}(W) using that finite local freeness of degree r is local on the target (step 5, from the existing finite/flat/lfp nodes). Second paragraph (quasi-compactness): for an affine W' in U_{r-1}, Z_r cap W' = V(I) and V(I) = V(I_lambda) for a finitely generated I_lambda via Limits 06AC (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-descend-finite-locally-free) applied to the limit Spec(A/I) = lim Spec(A/I_lambda); then U_r cap W is quasi-compact by induction, and S_r cap W is closed in the quasi-compact U_{r-1} cap W. Tags 07RY, 07RZ, 03J4, 03JA, 06AC verified in tags/tags. Mathlib: no stratification, no universally bounded fibres, no descent of finite (locally free) morphisms along limits (LeanSearch, LeanFinder, Loogle, grep).

lean.statement: theorem exists_closed_stratification_of_flat_quasiFinite {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [IsSeparated f] (hf : f.IsQuasiFinite) : ∃ Z : ℕ → Set S, Z 0 = ∅ ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, IsClosed (Z n)) ∧ Monotone Z ∧ Pairwise (fun r t : ℕ => Disjoint (Z (r + 1) \ Z r) (Z (t + 1) \ Z t)) ∧ (⋃ r : ℕ, Z (r + 1) \ Z r) = Set.univ ∧ (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : T ⟶ S) (r : ℕ), (pullback.snd f g).IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfDegree r ↔ Set.range g ⊆ Z (r + 1) \ Z r) ∧ (∀ (r : ℕ) (W : S.Opens), IsCompact (W : Set S) → IsCompact ((Z (r + 1) \ Z r) ∩ (W : Set S)))
